applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement, signed in 2012, subject to its applicable scope and implementation arrangements
Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement between the Mainland Area and the Taiwan Area, signed in 2010; not a comprehensive income-tax treaty

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act; Counter-Terrorism Financing Act; Company Act Article 22-1 and related regulations governing reporting of company information, directors, managers, major shareholders and ultimate beneficial ownership; Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering of Financial Institutions; and Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering of Lawyers, Accountants and Notaries. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, screen the parent, all direct and indirect shareholders, directors, responsible persons, authorized signatories, UBOs, financiers, landlords and material counterparties against United Nations Security Council sanctions, Taiwan domestic sanctions and terrorism lists, United States OFAC lists where relevant to the transaction or payment rails, and commercially maintained sanctions and adverse-media databases. Apply enhanced due diligence to politically exposed persons, their family members and known close associates; document source of wealth and source of funds; identify nominee, bearer-share, layered-company and state-affiliated ownership risks; obtain senior-management approval for PEP relationships; maintain screening records and periodic rescreening. U.S. sanctions may apply independently to U.S. persons, U.S.-dollar clearing, U.S.-origin technology or designated persons and are not displaced by Taiwan incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company, Business and Limited Partnership One-stop Service portal: https://gcis.nat.gov.tw/mainNew/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered Chinese company name must comply with Taiwan Company Act naming rules and be distinguishable from existing registered names. A foreign-language name may be used for commercial and branding purposes but does not replace the required Chinese registered name. English transliteration should be consistent with the approved Chinese name and corporate form. The proposed business scope must use the Taiwan Standard Industrial Classification and the wording accepted by the competent registration authority. Mainland political, governmental or jurisdictional terminology must not be used in a manner that creates confusion regarding governmental status, public authority or regulated institutional status.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, business or limited partnership name
Words implying a government agency, public enterprise, official authority or other public-law institution
Bank, banking, trust, insurance, securities, futures, financial institution, credit cooperative and other regulated-finance terms unless the required special licence and statutory approval exist
University, school, hospital, medical institution, charity, foundation and other regulated institutional terms unless legally authorized
Investment, securities, finance, leasing, pawn, employment agency, travel agency, telecommunications, energy and other industry-specific terms where use may imply a regulated activity
National, central, ministry, bureau, commission, authority, international or similar prestige or governmental terms where prior approval or additional justification is required
Words prohibited by the Company Act, sectoral licensing laws, public-order rules or the competent authority's name-review practice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File the name and business-scope pre-check electronically through the Department of Commerce one-stop portal. A successful reservation is generally effective for six months from approval; an extension should be requested before expiry and is subject to the applicable administrative rules and portal practice. If rejected, obtain the electronic rejection reason, compare the proposed name against the Company Act and sectoral naming rules, and first submit a corrected name or supplementary explanation through the portal. Where an appealable administrative disposition has been issued, file an administrative appeal with the competent superior administrative authority within the statutory period stated in the disposition, generally 30 days from service under Taiwan administrative-procedure rules. Preserve evidence of filing, reservation, rejection, similarity searches and any sectoral approval. A name challenge does not cure missing foreign-investment approval, food registration or premises-use authorization.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Taiwan company must maintain a registered address capable of receiving official service and supporting registration, tax and regulatory inspections. A pure virtual office with no lawful right to use the premises, no landlord consent, or no operational access is unsuitable. For a delivery-only multi-brand kitchen, the food-preparation premises must be an actual approved location with lawful zoning, food-business registration, hygiene controls, traceability records, storage and delivery arrangements. A serviced office may be acceptable for the holding or administrative address if the provider permits company registration and official inspection, but it cannot substitute for the licensed food-production premises. Uber Eats and DoorDash onboarding, payment-service providers and banks may require evidence of the actual operating location, food registration and tax registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No published statutory probability exists. For a newly established delivery-only food business using a physical kitchen, a prudent compliance estimate is medium to high: approximately 25% to 50% likelihood of an inspection, verification visit or documentary premises check during the first 12 months, with materially higher risk following a complaint, food-safety incident, inconsistent registration data, high-risk ownership finding or licence application. The estimate is not an official government statistic. Unannounced inspections may be conducted under applicable food-safety and local-government enforcement powers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Articles 98, 100, 108 and 387 (limited company incorporation, full payment of capital and registration); Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, Article 73; Regulations Governing the Permission of Investment in Taiwan from the People's Republic of China, Articles 4, 6 and 8; Food Safety and Sanitation Act, Articles 8 and 13; Fire Services Act, Articles 6 and 10; Environmental Impact Assessment Act, Article 5 and Enforcement Rules Schedules I and II.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業發展署) via the One-Stop Industrial and Business Registration Portal (公司與商業一站式線上申請作業); prior investment approval required from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議司).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書) together with the Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), filed electronically on the MOEA One-Stop Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum under the Company Act, but the total capital must be fully paid at incorporation (Article 100). For a mainland-China invested company, the Investment Commission requires paid-in capital adequate for the approved ghost-kitchen business plan, practically not less than NT$2,000,000. Capital must be remitted through approved cross-strait banking channels, deposited in the preparatory office's dedicated NT$ bank account (escrow-like control until registration), and verified by a Taiwan-certified public accountant before the registration application is filed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION of CN_WFOE_LTD adopted by unanimous written consent of the Inaugural Board on [date]. RESOLVED: (1) The Articles of Incorporation are adopted as presented and the paid-up capital of NT$[●] is fully subscribed and accepted from the sole Mainland shareholder; (2) the registered office of the Company shall be located at [●], Taiwan, as approved by the Investment Commission; (3) [●] is appointed Chairperson and [●] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each serving at the pleasure of the sole shareholder; and (4) the Chairperson, together with any director, is authorized to execute, file, and prosecute all registration, licensing, banking, and tax applications necessary for incorporation, including the food business registration and environmental clearance, before all competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議司), Taipei
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Mainland Investment Application (陸資投資申請書) through the MOEA online investment application system or in person; attach the ghost-kitchen business plan covering virtual brands, kitchen facility, capital deployment, Taiwanese employment and delivery-platform operations; execute the statutory declarations regarding source of funds, beneficial ownership and non-prohibited business items; pay the application review fee; await the Investment Approval Letter (投資許可函) which fixes the permitted business scope and the approved capital ceiling.
required_dossiers: Business plan for multi-brand delivery-only cloud kitchen
Investor's business license and articles of association from Mainland China (notarized per cross-strait notarization practice)
Investor's audited financial statements for the preceding fiscal year
Draft Articles of Incorporation of the Taiwan WFOE
Mainland investor declaration on source of funds, beneficial ownership and anti-money-laundering
Power of attorney and passport/ID copies of proposed Taiwan directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, the Commission issues a supplementary notice; submit the missing items within two months, with one possible six-month extension. If denied, cure the disqualifying factors and re-apply no earlier than six months from the denial; an administrative appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs may be filed within 30 days.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Taxation Administration (NTA), Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (R.O.C.); online portal: E-Tax Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw); local execution through regional national tax bureaus (國稅局) and revenue service offices (稽徵所).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — before incorporation, the Mainland China investor must obtain Taiwan investment approval from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; Step 2 — incorporate the WFOE as a Limited Liability Company through MOEA's Company Registration Online, receiving an 8-digit Unified Business Number (UBIN/統一編號) issued automatically by MOEA; Step 3 — complete mandatory tax registration with the local Revenue Service Office of NTA within 15 days after commencement of business under Article 28, Business Tax Act; Step 4 — exchange the UBIN for the Business Tax Registration Certificate and, if the WFOE carries on export activities, apply to the Taipei Customs, Customs Administration, for a Customs Exporter Code. For the Taiwan WFOE, the UBIN is the single statutory TIN/VAT ID and must be printed on all Uniform Invoices and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Taiwan WFOE is a taxable resident company incorporated under the Taiwan Company Act; it is taxed on worldwide income at the 20% Corporate Income Tax rate (with an additional 5% retained-earnings surtax on undistributed earnings at certain levels); it is not a pass-through or transparent entity; any distribution to the Mainland China shareholder is subject to withholding tax at the applicable rate under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement, subject to qualification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election is available under Taiwan law; statutory classification is factual, not elective. Available elections relevant to entity income tax include: (1) application for exemption of the retained-earnings surtax on reinvested income under the Statute for Industrial Innovation; (2) election by a foreign investor-owned WFOE to adopt a January-December fiscal year if the parent uses a different fiscal year, subject to NTA approval; (3) selection of the profit-contribution method under Article 25 of the Income Tax Act for deemed service income from international transactions; and (4) execution of an Advance Pricing Agreement (APA) or unilateral business tax rulings for cross-border related-party transactions. Tax treaties are not applicable to Mainland China investors except under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax (加值型營業稅) under the Taiwan Business Tax Act (營業稅法) — a VAT/GST-type indirect tax levied on taxable supplies of goods and services in Taiwan.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$0 registration threshold for a Taiwan-incorporated WFOE with a fixed place of business (e.g., a ghost kitchen facility); registration is mandatory as soon as the WFOE commences taxable sales. For an offshore foreign supplier without a Taiwan fixed place of business that sells only cross-border electronic services to Taiwanese consumers, the threshold is NT$480,000 in annual taxable sales from Taiwan-source services; the physical ghost-kitchen structure eliminates threshold applicability.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All sellers must issue sequential Uniform Invoices under Article 32 of the Business Tax Act; for delivery-only, multi-brand ghost kitchens, the WFOE must issue electronic Uniform Invoices (E-Invoice) or use an NTA-approved food-delivery platform (e.g., UberEats, DoorDash) that issues electronic receipts on the seller's behalf. The E-Invoice details must be transmitted through the government E-Invoice Platform digital API (Turnkey/API) within 48 hours after issuance; the system applies encrypted QR-code stamping and sequential invoice number clearance, but Taiwan does not implement a per-transaction government real-time approval. Failing to upload, using non-approved POS, or generating off-book numbers is a Business Tax Act violation punishable by one to five times the evaded tax.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act for: (i) goods physically exported from Taiwan to Mainland China or third countries, evidenced by Customs export declaration; and (ii) services supplied by the WFOE that are used or enjoyed wholly outside Taiwan, including offshore franchise/know-how, cloud-kitchen software/management, and delivery-platform ancillary services, provided the services are not substantially performed within Taiwan. The WFOE must be a general VAT taxpayer for the refund mechanism; input VAT on export-related purchases becomes creditable and refundable under Article 39, and export sales are reported on the quarterly Business Tax return at a zero rate rather than at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Collection Evidence (出口外匯收入水單)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Any fraudulent zero-rating claim, including forged customs declarations, fictitious Bills of Lading, or sham offshore service contracts, is subject to retrospective reassessment of the 5% Business Tax on the entire export sale, plus a penalty of one to five times the underpaid tax under Article 51, and a late-payment surcharge of 1.5% for every two days. The NTA and Customs Administration may issue joint audit examinations using UberEats/DoorDash payouts, cross-border payment rails, and Taiwan foreign-exchange settlement records. Criminal liability may arise under the Tax Collection Act and Criminal Code for tax evasion with imprisonment up to five years; refunds previously issued are clawed back with statutory interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, 国家外汇管理局) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC, 中国人民银行); regulated by the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations of the PRC (2008, as revised) and the SAFE '汇发' circular series; cross-border payments and capital-account registrations are executed bank-side under SAFE delegation and monitored through the 外汇局资本项目信息系统 and BOP (国际收支) direct reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is current-account convertible for genuine trade and service transactions under China's IMF Article VIII obligations, while capital-account transactions (equity injection, cross-border loans, dividend/principal repatriation) remain registration- and authenticity-based. A Taiwan-invested WFOE must complete the 外商投资信息报告 (foreign-investment information filing) with the market-regulation authority and bank-executed SAFE FDI registration (境内直接投资外汇登记) before receiving inbound equity. Profit remittance requires audited financial statements, corporate income tax settlement proof (完税证明), board resolution on profit distribution, and bank-side authenticity review under the '展业三原则' (KYC, authenticity, due diligence); unrestricted convertibility for speculative or non-trade flows is prohibited.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory export-proceeds surrender was abolished in 2012 (汇发〔2012〕20号); no statutory timeline or conversion ratio currently applies. Export/service-trade receipts must be credited to a registered 经常项目外汇账户 and reported under BOP rules before conversion to RMB beyond the registered intended use. For a delivery-only ghost-kitchen WFOE, platform payouts (Meituan/Ele.me) are domestic RMB and outside surrender rules; cross-border service receipts or royalties from the Taiwan parent or overseas licensees above USD 50,000 require a 服务贸易外汇业务办理表 and the tax-filing certificate (服务贸易等项目对外支付税务备案表) at the paying bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited (中国银行)
Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (中国工商银行)
China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. (招商银行)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Mainland-licensed digital banks (WeBank, MYBank) may open RMB settlement accounts only after physical KYC of the legal representative and cannot maintain SAFE capital-account escrow relationships for FDI; offshore EMIs (Airwallex, Currenxie, Payoneer) hold no CBIRC/SAFE banking license and cannot hold capital-account funds or perform onshore FX conversion for a PRC WFOE. A Taiwan parent may use offshore EMI accounts for treasury overlay, but all compliant inbound equity, outbound royalties, and platform settlements of the mainland WFOE must flow through a licensed Chinese commercial bank; cross-border e-commerce licensed payment institutions (LianLian, PingPong) are supplementary collection channels only and not a substitute for a corporate settlement account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandated: the legal representative and at least one beneficial owner of the Taiwan shareholder must attend the know-your-customer interview in person at a mainland branch (PBOC 银发〔2019〕41号; CBIRC AML rules). Remote video opening is generally not accepted for a capital-account escrow account or the basic deposit account (基本存款账户) of a newly formed WFOE; a bank due-diligence site visit to the ghost-kitchen premises is standard. If the Taiwan legal representative cannot travel, a mainland-appointed manager may be interviewed under a notarized and legalized power of attorney, but the Taiwan shareholder's identity documents must still be verified at account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a Taiwan-registered individual or holding company without mainland residence or verifiable local business presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association of the Taiwan shareholder; legalized shareholder resolution appointing the WFOE legal representative; ownership-chain diagram to ultimate natural persons; Taiwan compatriot permit (台胞证) and passport copies; proof of residential address; bank reference letters from the remitting Taiwan financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered business scope (营业执照) lacks explicit food-service or internet-catering permissions for a dark-kitchen operation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business license covering 餐饮服务 and 互联网食品经营; valid 食品经营许可证 for the kitchen site; signed rack agreements with Meituan/Ele.me delivery platforms; dark-kitchen lease contracts; food-safety control manual; site hygiene and fire-safety certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High anticipated volume of fragmented third-party platform payouts flowing into a single corporate account during the early operating stage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement statements and payout schedules; VAT invoices issued by the WFOE to platforms; bank mandate segregating operational vs capital accounts; AML transaction-monitoring thresholds aligned to 大额交易 reporting; evidence of a single-use operational account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated WFOE with no tax-filing history expecting inbound equity remittance within 90 days
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Incorporation file (营业执照, 章程, 外商投资信息报告回执, SAFE FDI registration receipt); board resolution with capital call calendar; Taiwan investor funds-source statement; tax registration certificate; capital-usage commitment letter confirming compliance with the negative-list restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mixed trade versus investment flows if the WFOE simultaneously pays royalties to the Taiwan parent and later remits dividends
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP/franchise license agreements supported by transfer-pricing documentation (同期资料); royalty calculation working papers; withholding tax payment receipts; current-account contracts; completed 服务贸易等项目对外支付税务备案表 for out-payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Taiwan parent remits via SWIFT MT103 (or CIPS for direct CNH) to the WFOE's SAFE-registered 资本金账户, quoting purpose code 621011 (Investment Capital / 股权投资款) and the FDI registration reference; the receiving bank verifies the SAFE FDI confirmation, 外商投资信息报告 receipt, and negative-list restrictions before crediting. Foreign-currency inbound funds are settled into RMB through a 结汇待支付账户 in accordance with the registered intended-use positive list. Where the Taiwan parent provides intercompany debt, a 外债 (cross-border loan) registration under PBOC macroprudential management (跨境融资宏观审慎管理) is required, including borrowing-contract registration and FX-hedging documentation; equity injection is preferred for the ghost-kitchen WFOE to reduce debt-service and repatriation risk.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for open-account and service-trade payments to the Taiwan parent (royalties, technology fees, management fees), supported by the 税务备案 table where the amount exceeds USD 50,000; (ii) documentary letters of credit or clean collection/DP for import of commercial kitchen equipment from third-country suppliers; (iii) domestic RMB rails (CNAPS 大额支付系统, 网上支付跨行清算系统) for procurement of raw materials and platform-operating expenses inside mainland China; (iv) CIPS for cross-border RMB royalty or supplier payments when counterparties agree to CNH settlement. All outbound FX conversions must be supported by authentic trade documents (invoices, contracts, customs declarations, delivery-platform statements) and reported under BOP rules with bank application of the 展业三原则.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: 远期结售汇 - physically settled forward FX contracts against real current-account or registered capital-account exposure
外汇掉期 - CNY/USD FX swaps for liquidity rebalancing and cash-flow timing mismatches
货币掉期 - cross-currency and interest-rate swaps (including structured forms) permitted only where a genuine underlying borrowing or investment exposure exists, e.g., on an intercompany 外债 facility
人民币外汇期权 - plain-vanilla FX options purchased from a licensed bank under a documented trade-risk mandate

Excluded onshore: CNH/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDF) are not permitted for PRC-resident entities; speculative FX trading and open-ended derivatives positions are prohibited under PBOC and SAFE derivative rules; all hedging must be mark-to-market tracked with underlying exposure evidence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and final tax payment (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (jurisdiction tax bureau of the registered head office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 31 of the year immediately following the close of the fiscal year; payment and e-filing must be completed by the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid tax exposed to daily postal-bank interest and an additional surcharge of up to 15% of the assessed amount; false understatement may trigger a penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax; persistent non-payment is referred for collection, which can restrain the company's business and bank accounts and lead to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of financial statements, business report and profit-distribution proposal by the annual general shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's shareholders' meeting; minutes retained at the registered office and available to MOEA auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; by June 30 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Competent authority can impose an administrative fine of NT$20,000–NT$100,000 on the responsible person, set a deadline for remedial calling, and ultimately apply for dissolution/strike-off after continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CPA-audited financial statements filed after shareholder approval for companies meeting the mandatory audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) via the Company Registration electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after approval by the shareholders' meeting, generally by July 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 under Company Act for late/non-filing; the competent authority may also require correction within a fixed period and suspend the acceptance of other registration matters.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, MOEA (electronic UBO registration); physical register held at the Taiwan head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any direct or indirect acquisition/disposal of a 25% or greater substantive interest; if no change occurs, no standalone annual filing is made, but the register must be presented and re-confirmed at the annual shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, false, or incomplete UBO disclosure can expose the company and responsible officers to NT$50,000–NT$500,000 administrative fines under company/money-laundering compliance rules, with correction orders and possible registration strike-off for deliberate non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding statement and payment-amount reconciliation filing (salary and other taxable performance payments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Withholding statements by January 31 of the following year; reconciliation data consolidated with the profit-seeking enterprise annual return filed by May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding-agent penalties range from 5% to 20% of the unreported withholding amount plus daily interest; aggravated cases may be referred to criminal tax treatment and responsible officers can be debarred from service.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan limited company must produce independent CPA-audited financial statements if paid-in capital at the balance-sheet date exceeds NT$30 million, if it is a public/FSC-regulated company, or if the competent authority specially requires an audit under Company Act Article 20; a small ghost-kitchen WFOE kept below NT$30 million paid-in capital and not FSC-regulated remains audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Business Entity Accounting Act and the Business Entity Accounting Standards (enterprise accounting standards, EAS/GAAP) for non-public companies; IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission applies to public companies; statements must be prepared in New Taiwan Dollars and include balance sheet, comprehensive income statement, changes in equity, and cash-flow statement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a separate calendar-year UBO renewal filing if no substantive-control change occurs. A person holding, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the shares or voting rights (or exercising significant control) must be recorded in the Register of Substantial Controllers; any acquisition, transfer, or loss of such interest must be filed with MOEA within 15 days of the triggering event. At each annual shareholders' meeting, management must verify the register's completeness and note the verification in the minutes; the register remains inspectable at the registered office by government examiners and authorized third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,200 per year for a Taipei registered-office address and local corporate secretarial/agent retainer
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800–6,500 per annual cycle for a small non-public limited company subject to Taiwan CPA-audit requirements
